clue.text: Spacecraft with top the United States returned to the French

parts.note: a cap is the top or lid of something

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the country's initials are read from right to left

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for the country
le is the masculine 'the' in French; 'to' simply adds it on

explanation.surface: A spacecraft topped with a US flag heads back towards France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is a noun for a lid here, not the summit of the craft; le is French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule is the small crewed module of a rocket that carries astronauts and returns to Earth.

clue.text: Some people cause havoc adorning a pear tree

parts.note: surface padding, giving no letters

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the words that follow are wanted, a run lifted from inside them

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the two words, after the h and before the rning

explanation.surface: Some people make a nuisance of themselves decorating a pear tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people cause' is surface padding; the answer hides in havoc adorning. The fruit is also called the avocado pear or alligator pear.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a tropical tree whose fruit is commonly called the avocado pear, so the tree is fairly a pear tree.

clue.text: Frown from under small hood

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed under another simply follows it in the column

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: Someone glowers from beneath a little hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl is an angry, sullen facial expression, the same look as a frown with furrowed brows.

clue.text: Crustacean throws note into river

indicators.note: the musical piece runs into the waterway, so the two sit side by side in the column

parts.note: to lob is to throw something in a high arc
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A shellfish hurls a scrap of paper into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' is not a container here: TE flows into R by sitting just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large clawed marine shellfish, one of the decapod crustaceans.

clue.text: Care about time to produce space

indicators.note: turned about, the letters of the first word are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the four letters of care rearranged
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Taking care over the timing gives you room to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an amount of land measured in acres, an area or extent of ground, hence space.

clue.text: Church only organised in Sri Lanka once

indicators.note: organising things means arranging them, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the four letters of only rearranged

explanation.surface: A church that was only set up in Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylon was the colonial name of the island nation until it was renamed in 1972, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Burrowing invertebrate found in other warm form

indicators.note: the letters take another form, so they are rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: all nine letters of the two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature that digs has been discovered in a different, warmer shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The common garden worm tunnels through soil and has no backbone, so it is a digging spineless animal.

clue.text: Deer must laze around with broken leg

indicators.note: moved around, these letters are jumbled into another order
something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: An injured deer has no choice but to lie about with its broken leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are scrambled together into one seven-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a slender antelope; the clue loosely calls it a deer, a looser fit than a strict zoologist would allow.

clue.text: Loss of a diaper can cause an illusion of happiness

indicators.note: the letters are said to produce something new, being reworked to cause a different phrase

parts.note: all thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing a nappy can leave a baby falsely content.
explanation.walkthrough: A diaper is the American word for a nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a state of contentment based on false beliefs, contented ignorance that cannot last.

clue.text: Hello! Hello! — here's a toy!

parts.note: yo is a slangy greeting
the same greeting again

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully calls out twice while handing over a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is the spinning plaything on a string that climbs back up to the hand.

clue.text: Silly fool to treasure wooden spoon

parts.note: a booby is a stupid person
to prize something is to treasure it

explanation.surface: A daft person treasures an old kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the wooden spoon is the joke award for coming last.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases name a mock award handed to whoever finishes last in a competition.

clue.text: Little piece of pork for Prince of Denmark?

parts.note: ham is cured meat from a pig's leg
-let is a suffix making things small, as in piglet or booklet

explanation.surface: Offering a small slice of pork to a Danish royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the name as a tiny ham, the suffix -let meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Danish royal heir whose father is murdered by Claudius.

clue.text: Playing polo by hollow is way out

indicators.note: playing with something lets it be moved around freely into a new order

parts.note: the four letters of polo rearranged
a hole is a hollow or cavity

explanation.surface: A polo match next to a dip in the ground gives an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in rules that lets someone escape an obligation, figuratively an exit or escape route.

clue.text: Study screenplay, then enrol

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
a screenplay is a film's script

explanation.surface: An actor reads the screenplay and then signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript is to compel someone into military service, signing them up on the army's register.

clue.text: Patience is only stretched by Italian attitude

indicators.note: something stretched around another thing wraps it, so the first word goes outside the others

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
IT is a short form of Italian, as in It vermouth
an air is a manner or attitude, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone's patience is only tested by an Italian's attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like a virtue being tested; it is the card game, and 'stretched' means one word is pulled open around the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the British name for the card game played alone, known in America as solitaire.

clue.text: Witches gathering by inlet to the north

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Witches meet beside a little bay up in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is an assembly of witches, traditionally thirteen, meeting together for rites.

clue.text: Shoot dog

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to follow someone persistently

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an order to fire at a dog, but both words are separate meanings: a noun for a plant and a verb for following.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the main stem of a plant and a verb for following prey or a person secretly.

clue.text: New re-count results in defeat

indicators.note: a new version of the word has its letters made over in another order

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh recount of the votes ends in a loss for the candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat an opponent decisively, a heavy and thorough win over them.

clue.text: Medical care for mate floundering in the river

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands

indicators.note: something floundering is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the four letters of mate jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend struggling in a river needs a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: TRE(ATME)NT: the scrambled word goes inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the care a doctor gives a patient, the therapy or management of an illness.

clue.text: Guerrilla loses money to become craftsman

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a partisan is an irregular resistance fighter
p is a penny, as in 50p

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter goes broke and takes up a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the penny from the start of the fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand, such as a carpenter or potter.

clue.text: Pasta for the weak?

parts.note: surface reading: soft food suitable for invalids
setter's reading: a limp, feeble person is likened to a strand of cooked pasta, so the pasta is a name for weaklings

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a pun: the strands are limp, and a weak person is said to be like one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: They are long thin strands of pasta, notoriously floppy once cooked, matching the idea of feebleness.

clue.text: Bacon the artist's girl

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist, plus the 's
her stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon, the painter, and his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon looks like the painter Francis Bacon; it is breakfast bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a single thin slice of bacon or ham, cut for frying or grilling.

clue.text: In short, a PC form of communication

parts.note: surface reading: briefly, a personal computer as a means of communicating
setter's reading: PC is the standard abbreviation for the thing wanted, a card sent by mail

explanation.walkthrough: PC wants to be a computer or political correctness; here it is the short form of a picture card sent through the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard is a card with a message sent through the mail without an envelope, a way of keeping in touch.

clue.text: Habitat too peaceful to include military display

indicators.note: the words are said to include the answer, holding it within their letters

parts.note: the run sits across the two words, after habi
surface padding, giving no letters

explanation.surface: A habitat too tranquil to host an army show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peaceful' is surface padding. A tattoo is an evening military display of drumming and marching, as at Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an outdoor military entertainment of marching bands and drill, like the Edinburgh event.

clue.text: Compact arrangement of trees

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things out in a chosen order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A neat, tight grouping of trees in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and to the point, using few words, so it is concise or compact.

clue.text: The opposite position taken against the half-sister

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the second part dropped

parts.note: anti means opposed to
taken as written
taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: Someone takes the contrary stance against their half-sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-sister looks like a family relation, but means the first half of sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition, and its antithesis is the contrasting proposition set against it, the reverse view.

clue.text: Depend on really, when nearly all is lost

indicators.note: nearly the whole of a word means it stops one letter short of its end
what is lost is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
all cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Counting on someone, truly, when almost everything has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AL out of REALLY to leave RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to trust them or count on them for support, the same as depend.

clue.text: Ever gone back on large railway? It's fun!

indicators.note: something gone back has retraced its route, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written before turning
L is the clothing-label abbreviation for large
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A question about a trip back on a big railway line, enjoyed by all.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively, noisy celebration and merrymaking, high spirits and partying of a fun kind.

clue.text: Scene in "Tempest" will infuriate

indicators.note: a tempest is a violent storm, which throws the letters about into chaos

parts.note: all seven letters of the two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A scene in Shakespeare's play The Tempest will enrage its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The play title looks like a source, but it is the storm that jumbles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone, stressed on the second syllable, is to make them very angry or enraged.
